gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 5?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather models, including GFS and ICON runs, indicate a highest temperature near 24°C in Munich on September 5, driven by moderate westerly flow and partial clearing after morning showers. This aligns with trader emphasis on 24°C (62.5% implied probability) and nearby 23–25°C outcomes, as ensemble guidance shows limited variability around the seasonal norm of roughly 21°C. Recent observations confirm no strong ridge or cold advection altering the pattern, with dew points and pressure trends supporting modest afternoon warming before evening cooling. Updated high-resolution forecasts and official DWD guidance expected overnight will further refine peak values ahead of market resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance points to a 23°C maximum for London on September 5 under generally fine conditions with sunny spells and lightening westerly winds, supporting the near-even market split between 22°C and 23°C. High pressure and reduced cloud cover should promote strong daytime heating, while the light flow limits cooler maritime influence and keeps the urban heat island effect modest. Ensemble guidance shows minor spread in afternoon cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing that could trim or add 1°C, creating the tight probabilities. Updated model runs tomorrow morning and official Met Office briefings will refine the exact peak before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on September 5, 2026, centers on 22–23°C as the leading outcomes (39% and 49% implied probability), reflecting model consensus from official forecasts for a moderate peak under high pressure.**

Persistent high pressure over the UK has produced clear to partly cloudy skies with light westerly winds, enabling typical early-September daytime heating without significant cloud cover or strong advection of cooler air. Met Office guidance and ensemble outputs consistently indicate a daytime maximum of 22°C, with some runs reaching 23°C during peak afternoon hours around 14:00–16:00 local time; minimums overnight were near 13–15°C. This aligns with climatological norms for early September in London (around 20–22°C), following a brief cooler spell earlier in the week.

No major model disagreements or unexpected developments, such as unexpected frontal activity or enhanced solar radiation, have emerged to shift probabilities toward 24°C or higher, keeping those outcomes below 10%. The tight spread between 22°C and 23°C underscores genuine uncertainty in the precise peak, resolvable only by official station readings (e.g., Heathrow or central London sites) once the full diurnal cycle completes. Traders are weighting the most recent short-range guidance, which favors the 22–23°C band as the skin-in-the-game consensus.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble model consensus position a mid-70s°F high as the most likely outcome for New York City on September 6, driving the 40.5% implied probability on 76-77°F and 25% on 74-75°F. Northeasterly flow advecting cooler maritime air, combined with partial cloud cover and light winds, is suppressing daytime heating below the 1991-2020 climatological average of 79.5°F. Official point forecasts from the New York National Weather Service office indicate a 75°F maximum, consistent with recent GFS and other guidance runs showing limited diurnal warming. The 22.5% market weight on 78-79°F reflects residual uncertainty in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing, while lower-probability bins account for possible model shifts ahead of the final observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including DWD-MOS and ECMWF guidance, indicate a post-frontal high-pressure setup over southern Germany after widespread rain and thunderstorms on September 5. This pattern supports mostly clear skies, light northeasterly winds, and efficient daytime heating on September 6, with afternoon maxima centered near 23–25°C. Historical climatology places the September 6 average high at 21.2°C, but the current ridge and reduced cloud cover elevate expectations modestly above baseline without pushing into late-summer extremes. Market-implied odds clustering at 24°C (51.5%) with secondary support at 23°C and 25°C reflect tight model consensus on this range, with low probabilities assigned to outliers given stable steering patterns and limited moisture return. Updated short-range runs tomorrow morning will provide the final confirmation ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble model consensus position a mid-70s°F high as the most likely outcome for New York City on September 6, driving the 40.5% implied probability on 76-77°F and 25% on 74-75°F. Northeasterly flow advecting cooler maritime air, combined with partial cloud cover and light winds, is suppressing daytime heating below the 1991-2020 climatological average of 79.5°F. Official point forecasts from the New York National Weather Service office indicate a 75°F maximum, consistent with recent GFS and other guidance runs showing limited diurnal warming. The 22.5% market weight on 78-79°F reflects residual uncertainty in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing, while lower-probability bins account for possible model shifts ahead of the final observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain, and northerly winds are suppressing daytime heating across the Tokyo region on September 6, keeping maximum temperatures well below the late-summer climatological normal of roughly 29 °C. Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and multiple numerical weather models converge on a high near 24–25 °C under overcast skies and steady precipitation, with only modest uncertainty arising from the precise timing of any brief cloud breaks or shifts in wind direction that could allow slightly more insolation. These conditions produce the tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 23–26 °C, as traders weigh small differences in forecast details that determine whether the daily peak registers at the lower or upper end of that narrow range.

Westerly flow, morning cloud cover, and scattered showers (with probabilities ranging 30–90% early in the day) are limiting daytime heating, while afternoon clearing under building high pressure supports peaks near 23–24°C (roughly 73–75°F). This is modestly above the 1991–2020 September 5 average high of 21.4°C but well below historical extremes like 30.1°C. 

Hourly guidance from multiple agencies shows temperatures rising from morning lows around 11–17°C to afternoon maxima of 23–24°C before evening cooling, with limited model spread keeping 25°C or higher at low odds. Traders' skin-in-the-game consensus thus centers on these values ahead of final observational data.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 6?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 5?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current short-range forecast models from agencies including DWD and ECMWF indicate a peak temperature in Munich on September 7 most likely between 26–29 °C, driven by building high pressure, light southerly or westerly flow, and partly cloudy skies that permit strong diurnal heating while limiting excessive insolation. Scattered afternoon convection could cap the maximum if showers develop earlier than modeled, or allow readings near the upper end under clearer conditions; ensemble spreads and local urban heat effects create the tight clustering around 27 °C (market-implied 34 %). Historical September 7 averages near 21 °C underscore the anomalous warmth, with resolution depending on the final 48-hour model updates and observed maximum at the official station.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Met Office guidance points to a 26°C maximum in London on September 6 under southerly winds and partly cloudy skies, with hourly peaks near 25°C by mid-afternoon. This aligns with model consensus showing above-average warmth for early September, when the climatological high is 21°C, driven by a temporary ridge favoring warmer advection rather than strong insolation. Other sources range from 24–27°C, reflecting typical short-range forecast spread in temperature and cloud cover. Trader positioning, with 26°C at 41.5% implied probability ahead of 25°C and 27°C, closely tracks this ensemble view, while lower odds on extremes reflect limited potential for rapid intensification or cooling ahead of the next frontal system. Updated model runs and official briefings tomorrow morning will refine resolution criteria.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in NYC on September 5?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the National Weather Service and major models points to a daily maximum of 80–82°F in New York City on September 5, 2026, under sunny skies and light northerly winds.** This aligns closely with the market’s heavy weighting toward the 80–81°F bin (67% implied probability) and the secondary 78–79°F outcome (23%).

Morning observations showed temperatures in the low 70s with partly cloudy conditions and northwest flow around 5–10 mph, consistent with post-frontal stabilization that limits afternoon heating. The long-term September 5 average high at Central Park is 79.8°F, so today’s expected reading sits slightly above normal but well below the extreme records near 94°F. Ensemble guidance shows minimal spread, with little risk of significant model divergence or late-day convective development that could push readings into the mid-80s.

Traders are therefore pricing the most likely observed maximum—measured at official stations such as Central Park or LaGuardia— squarely in the low 80s, with only modest probability assigned to a slightly cooler or warmer realization depending on exact peak timing and micro-scale variations.

**Forecast models and real-time observations position 24°C and 25°C as the leading outcomes for Munich’s daily maximum on September 5, 2026, with market-implied probabilities of 61% and 35%.** 

Official guidance from the Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) and consensus across GFS-based ensembles indicate maxima between 21–26°C under westerly flow, with afternoon clearing after morning showers or variable cloud cover allowing temperatures to peak near or slightly above the long-term September 5 average high of 21.4°C. Hourly data show readings climbing from around 18°C midday toward 23–25°C by mid-afternoon before declining, consistent with light-to-moderate winds (10–20 km/h) and modest humidity that limit further warming. 

Recent model runs and surface observations confirm no significant deviation from this narrow band, though minor shifts in cloud timing or localized showers could still nudge the exact high within the 23–25°C window. Historical precedent for the date includes occasional warmer spikes above 27°C, but current synoptic conditions favor the tighter cluster now reflected in trader positioning.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance positions a 26°C maximum as the leading outcome for London on September 6, citing southerly winds advecting warmer air after morning cloud and rain clear to allow afternoon sunshine. This places the day several degrees above the 1991–2020 average high of 21°C for the date. Multiple numerical models show close agreement on peak values between 24–27°C, with limited spread tied to exact cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing. Traders have concentrated probability on 26°C (48.5%) and the adjacent 25°C/27°C bins, reflecting both the central forecast and typical observational uncertainty of ±1°C at urban stations such as Heathrow. No significant revisions have emerged in the latest model runs.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Met Office and European centers indicate a peak temperature near 23–24°C for London on September 7, driven by a transient ridge of high pressure yielding mostly dry, partly cloudy conditions with moderate southwesterly winds. Recent warming, including a projected 26°C on September 6, reflects residual warm advection ahead of an approaching Atlantic front that introduces increasing cloud cover and a slight cooling trend by Monday afternoon. Ensemble spreads remain tight around these values, with minor differences in timing of maximum insolation and boundary-layer mixing explaining the near-even market split between 23°C and 24°C. Updated model runs and observational data through the weekend will refine exact highs ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the UK Met Office and supporting models indicate a maximum of 21–23°C for London on September 5 under high pressure, with sunny intervals, light westerly winds, and minimal cloud cover limiting further warming. Midday observations near 22°C align with this range, while climatological September averages hover around 17–19°C. Model consensus shows little divergence, though slight variations in timing of any coastal showers or wind shifts could nudge the daily peak. Traders have priced 23°C as the leading outcome at 61.5% implied probability, followed by 22°C at 28%, reflecting the narrow forecast spread and proximity to resolution.

This aligns with early September climatology, where the long-term average high is about 21°C, but current steering patterns and modest instability have kept temperatures from exceeding the mid-20s. Live data through mid-afternoon show readings holding at or just below 24°C, reducing odds of a 25°C or higher peak while supporting the narrow 23–24°C range as the most probable outcome before evening cooling.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated Met Office guidance and final station observations will determine resolution.

High humidity and reduced insolation from persistent overcast skies tend to cap daytime peaks, while any breaks in rain could allow brief warming toward the upper end of the range. Recent model runs have narrowed slightly but still diverge on the precise maximum, consistent with the market’s near-even split among the top three outcomes. Official updates from the Japan Meteorological Agency and new global model cycles over the next 24–48 hours will likely provide the clearest resolution signal ahead of the day itself.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from National Weather Service models places New York City’s September 5 high near the 79–81 °F range, driven by a northerly wind shift that advected cooler, drier air behind earlier humid conditions. Light north-northwest winds of 5–10 mph and mostly sunny skies are limiting afternoon boundary-layer mixing and surface heating, keeping peak temperatures close to the early-September climatological average of roughly 80 °F at LaGuardia. Ensemble spread centers on whether mixing reaches the 80–81 °F bin or remains capped in the upper 70s, producing the near-even market split between those two outcomes and minimal probability for extremes outside 76–83 °F. Updated model runs and afternoon observations will determine final resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast uncertainty from an approaching frontal system and heavy rain is keeping trader consensus tightly clustered around 26–28°C for Tokyo’s September 7 high.** Multiple models show a southerly flow ahead of widespread showers and thunderstorms, with highs most often projected between 26°C and 29°C depending on exact timing of cloud cover and precipitation. High humidity and reduced insolation from persistent overcast skies tend to cap daytime peaks, while any breaks in rain could allow brief warming toward the upper end of the range. Recent model runs have narrowed slightly but still diverge on the precise maximum, consistent with the market’s near-even split among the top three outcomes. Official updates from the Japan Meteorological Agency and new global model cycles over the next 24–48 hours will likely provide the clearest resolution signal ahead of the day itself.
